$comment: These are regression-safety budgets for deterministic headless browser journeys, not product SLAs.
They intentionally detect hangs, missing output, interaction breakage, and extreme instability.
They must never be used to claim performance superiority over another SDK.
schemaVersion 2 (issue #562) adds staged scale-tier metrics, a 100k/1M row scale corpus, and repeated
mount/unmount + context-loss recovery leak budgets. BOTH scale tiers (deckgl.scale-render-100k and
deckgl.scale-render-1m) are opt-in (HONUA_BROWSER_BENCH_SCALE=full / npm run bench:browser:full-scale) and
excluded from the deterministic PR lane's default `npm run bench:browser` run; only the 10k
deckgl.binary-render-interact scenario, the capability scenarios, and the lifecycle scenarios run there.
The 100k and 1M entries below were reviewed on 2026-08-01 from three serialized Full-Scale Evidence runs
on the same a0b3aecd commit, GitHub ubuntu24 runner class, Chromium 145, and SwiftShader renderer:
runs 30716684349, 30717019856, and 30717020832. Across-run coefficient of variation was 7.2-12.0% for
first frame, interaction/picking, GPU upload, conversion, and steady FPS. Every run preserved zero copied
payload bytes, passed its journey invariants, and reported 37.3 MB heap after the 1M first frame.
Warning thresholds leave approximately 25-50% headroom for first-frame, interaction/picking, GPU-upload,
and steady-FPS runner variance; faster conversion, transfer, and disposal stages retain wider absolute margins.
Failure thresholds identify hangs or material regressions rather than normal shared-runner noise.
SwiftShader is a CPU software rasterizer, so these remain regression-safety budgets, not device SLAs.
stage metrics ending in Ms are upper bounds (smaller is better); steadyFrameRateFps is a lower bound
(direction: at-least) since a smaller frames-per-second value is the regression.
